## The Alpha Label Means Something

Claude Flow requires installation with `npx claude-flow@alpha`. That **@alpha** tag isn't decorative - it's a clear signal that this is actively being built, in public, in real-time.

## What Alpha Actually Means

**Alpha is not a label for broken. It's a signal of active development.**

- ✅ It means I'm building fast and sharing early
- ✅ It means features are evolving daily  
- ✅ It means some parts are stubs waiting to be implemented
- ✅ It means you're watching the creative process unfold
- ❌ It does NOT mean it should be production-complete

## The Real

items.author: HF-teamdev
items.body:
Anthropic just mass-dropped Opus 4.6 — and it ships with **native Agent Teams** baked into Claude Code. Multiple agents, parallel execution, autonomous coordination. Sound familiar?

That's claude-flow's core pitch. As of today, Anthropic does it out of the box.

**This isn't a death sentence — it's an inflection point.** The features Opus 4.6 *doesn't* ship with are exactly where claude-flow can become indispensable. But the window to pivot is now, not later.

I spent several hours analyzing the full claude-flow v3 codebase (175+ MCP tools, 20 ADRs, 22 tool modules) against every new Opus 4.6
items.title: Opus 4.6 Just Shipped Native Agent Teams — Here's 28 Ways Claude-Flow Becomes Indispensable
